over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented

# Outcome sub-dossier — State National Companies realized record after the Markel acquisition, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> the transaction was structured at closing. The outcome window is fixed as the ~3-5
> years following the ~2017 closing (approximately 2020-2022); because the registrant
> was absorbed and deregistered, there is no separate audited public financial record
> for this entity in that window, and the outcome is coded uncertain per the no-record
> rule, documented only to the extent public filings establish it.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction
- State National's last annual report as an independent registrant was its Form 10-K
  filed 2017-03-14, covering fiscal year 2016. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-17-001763, Form 10-K]
- State National filed a Form 15-12B (Certification and Notice of Termination of
  Registration) on 2017-12-01, terminating its duty to file reports under the Securities
  Exchange Act of 1934; the filing states the approximate number of holders of record as
  of the certification date was 1. [SRC: SEC accession 0001610793-17-000007, Form 15-12B]
- No annual report (Form 10-K) was filed by State National as an independent registrant
  after fiscal year 2016; consequently no audited public financial statements exist for
  State National as a standalone entity within the ~2020-2022 outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001610793-17-000007, Form 15-12B]

## Acquirer's separate disclosure of the acquired business (qualitative)
- In its Form 10-K for fiscal year 2020 (filed 2021-02-19), Markel Corporation describes
  a "State National division" within its Insurance segment, stating that the Insurance
  segment "is written through our Markel Specialty, Markel International and State
  National divisions, with the exception of our State National division's program
  services business, which is not included in a reportable segment." [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-21-000032, Form 10-K FY2020]
- The same filing states that "the State National division writes collateral protection
  insurance, which insures personal automobiles and other vehicles held as collateral
  for loans made by credit unions, banks and specialty finance companies through its
  lender services product line," and that its program services business "generates fee
  income, in the form of ceding (program service) fees, by offering issuing carrier
  capacity" to third parties, and is "separately managed from our underwriting
  divisions...in order to protect our program services customers and eliminate internal
  competition." [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-21-000032, Form 10-K FY2020]
- In its Form 10-K for fiscal year 2022 (filed 2023-02-17), Markel again describes "the
  State National division writes collateral protection insurance in the U.S." and
  states "the results of our program services operations are not included in a
  reportable segment," using materially the same description as the FY2020 filing.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-23-000033, Form 10-K FY2022]
- Both the FY2020 and FY2022 Markel Form 10-K filings list the same set of underwriting
  subsidiaries (City National Insurance Company, Independent Specialty Insurance
  Company, National Specialty Insurance Company, State National Insurance Company, Inc.,
  and United Specialty Insurance Company) as the entities through which the program
  services business continues to be written. [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-21-000032, Form 10-K FY2020] [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-23-000033, Form 10-K FY2022]

## Absence of a separately quantified financial trajectory
- Neither the FY2020 nor the FY2022 Markel Form 10-K discloses a segment-level or
  entity-level revenue, net income, premium-volume, or other quantified financial figure
  specific to the State National division or its constituent subsidiaries as distinct
  from Markel's consolidated or Insurance-segment totals; both filings explicitly state
  that the program services results are "not included in a reportable segment."
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-21-000032, Form 10-K FY2020] [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-23-000033, Form 10-K FY2022]
- Whether any other separately quantified trajectory for the acquired business (e.g., a
  standalone revenue or earnings figure) exists in a source not retrieved for this
  dossier was not established. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- State National Companies, Inc. operated as an independent SEC registrant through
  fiscal year 2016, was acquired by Markel Corporation, and deregistered its common
  stock via a Form 15-12B filed 2017-12-01 reporting a single holder of record;
  consequently there is no separate audited public 3-5-year financial record for State
  National as a standalone entity. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-17-001763, Form 10-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001610793-17-000007, Form 15-12B]
- Markel's own Form 10-K filings for fiscal years 2020 and 2022 separately describe a
  continuing "State National division" performing the same collateral-protection and
  program-services (fronting) business lines through the same named underwriting
  subsidiaries, but disclose no segment- or entity-level quantified financial trajectory
  for that division specifically; the outcome over the fixed window is therefore coded
  uncertain on any quantified scalar, documented only by this qualitative operational
  continuity rather than fabricated or inferred from Markel's consolidated results.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-21-000032, Form 10-K FY2020] [SRC: SEC accession 0001096343-23-000033, Form 10-K FY2022]

[SLICE END]
